final_answer:
Based on FY2024 net income figures for each company:

- Delta: $3,457M [DOC-1]
- United: $3,149M [DOC-1]
- American: $846M [DOC-1]
- Southwest: $465M [DOC-1]
- Alaska: $395M [DOC-1]

Note on comparability: Alaska's FY2024 results are not fully comparable to prior periods or to a "steady-state" airline of similar size because they include only a partial-year contribution from its September 18, 2024 acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings — Hawaiian contributed $869M of revenue and a $113M net loss for the ~3.5 months it was consolidated [DOC-2]. This means Alaska's reported net income of $395M reflects a one-time acquisition drag and a stub-period consolidation of Hawaiian, not a full year of combined operations, so it is not an apples-to-apples comparison with the other four airlines' full-year, non-acquisition-affected results. This caveat does not change the ranking outcome, however, since Delta's net income exceeds all others by a wide margin regardless of this adjustment.

All five companies report on the same calendar fiscal year (Jan 1–Dec 31, 2024) [DOC-1], so the basic net income comparison across Delta, United, Southwest, and American is directly comparable; only Alaska's figure carries the acquisition caveat noted above.

Using net income as the profitability measure, Delta Air Lines had the highest net income among the five carriers in FY2024.

ANSWER: Delta Air Lines (FY2024 net income of $3,457 million, the highest among Delta, United, Southwest, American, and Alaska)
